      Crystal Palace Academy Graduates

      Crystal Palace's Academy has produced stars throughout the generations, from early youth team graduates like Johnny Byrne to '80s legends Kenny Sansom and Vince Hilaire, to modern day icons like Wilfried Zaha and England manager Gareth Southgate.

      In recent years that lineage has continued, with a roster of players starting their careers in south London before thriving at the club and elsewhere.

      In fact, since the turn of the millennium, Palace’s Academy has produced over 50 players to compete competitively in the first-team.

      Among those are names like Wayne Routledge, Ben Watson, John Bostock, Victor Moses, Jonny Williams, as well as current Palace men Nathaniel Clyne and Tyrick Mitchell.

      More recently, a UEFA Conference League visit from KuPS Kuopio marked another statement night for the Academy, as George King, Dean Benamar and Joel Drakes-Thomas all made their senior debuts on the European stage.

      It was the first time three Academy graduates had started a first-team match together, and the youngest Palace XI fielded since 1982.

      With a Category 1 setup and youth teams competing at the very top across all age groups, you can be sure there are even more to come.
